limitations: Cross-dataset evaluation: YOLOPv2 was trained on BDD100K, whose 'drivable area' label covers the directly drivable lane plus alternative (adjacent, same-direction or opposite) lanes, while KITTI 'road' is the whole road surface (composition of all lanes). The labelling conventions differ (e.g. parking strips, road edges, sidewalk-level surfaces), so part of the measured error is convention mismatch, not model error.

KITTI images are about 1242x375 (aspect 3.3:1). The production letterbox policy (longest side 640, stride-32 minimal padding) turns them into a 640x224 canvas of 640x193 content; BDD100K training frames are 16:9, so the model sees an unusually wide, low-resolution canvas it was not trained on.

Metrics are computed in the perspective image space at the service's fixed binary operating point. They are NOT the official KITTI Road benchmark result, which is MaxF (F-measure maximised over a confidence sweep) evaluated in a 800x400 bird's-eye-view grid ([-10 m, 10 m] lateral, [6 m, 46 m] longitudinal, 0.05 m cells). Perspective space weights near-field pixels far more heavily than BEV does. Do not compare these numbers with the KITTI leaderboard.

Training split only (the only KITTI split with public labels; 289 images, three urban categories um/umm/uu, Karlsruhe, Germany, daylight). YOLOPv2 never trained on KITTI and nothing was tuned on these images, but the split is small and geographically narrow; it says nothing about night, rain, highways or other countries.
Licence: KITTI is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (non-commercial). The images and labels are used for this local measurement only and are not redistributed; only file names and SHA256 hashes are committed.

Lane-marking accuracy is NOT evaluated: KITTI um_lane ground truth is the ego-lane AREA, not lane markings, and YOLOPv2 has no ego-lane output. YOLOPv2 vehicle detection is not evaluated here either (KITTI Road has no boxes).
KITTI training images are lossless PNG; they are encoded once as JPEG q95 before inference (same as the video pipeline), so results include one lossy compression step.
GT 'don't care' pixels (R plane == 0) are excluded from all counts, following the devkit. Predictions inside those regions are neither true nor false positives.

The service ran the YOLOPv2 + RF-DETR-N ensemble; the drivable mask is produced by YOLOPv2 alone, so model_sha256 is the YOLOPv2 checkpoint and the ensemble identity is recorded in details. Service latency includes both models.

protocol.input: KITTI image_2 PNG -> RGB -> JPEG q95 (app.video.encode.encode_jpeg_bytes, as the video pipeline) -> POST /v1/infer via app.perception.client.InferenceClient
protocol.prediction: drivable_mask_png (YOLOPv2 seg head argmax == 1, unletterboxed to the original frame by the service) > 127
protocol.space: original perspective image space (no bird's-eye-view transform)
protocol.dataset_level: sum of per-image TP/FP/FN over images, then ratios
protocol.per_image: ratios per image; images with TP+FP+FN == 0 have undefined IoU and are excluded from the per-image distribution
